public_rationale: In its July 29, 2026 earnings call, Meta reported advertising-performance gains from AI systems during April–June 2026, an application outside the excluded rentals to Anthropic and OpenAI [e1]. The disclosure does not isolate GPU-attributable benefits after costs or measure the broad economic contribution of included GPU uses [e1]. Meta's October 13 technical disclosure documents GPU training for its GEM recommendation model, but does not establish quarter-specific value or what prospective evidence was available on September 1 [e2]. Together, these disclosures do not settle whether the included uses generated 'very little' economic value or whether there were few credible signs of future value at publication [e1, e2].
limitations: The commercial and technical evidence is company-reported, without matched independent measurements.
Advertising-performance gains do not directly measure net economic value.
The packet lacks representative measurements across the included GPU uses.
The claim supplies no numerical threshold for 'very little'; April–June 2026 is the contract's chosen assessment period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Outside rentals to Anthropic and OpenAI, AI GPUs generate very little economic value, with few signs that will change.
conditions: outside of rentals to Anthropic and OpenAI

statement.excerpt: AI GPUs are, outside of rentals to Anthropic and OpenAI, generating very little economic value, and there are few signs that they will do so in the future outside of anecdotes and copium.

from_speaker: outside of rentals to Anthropic and OpenAI
few signs that they will do so in the future
our_interpretation: Read economic value as demonstrated commercial benefits, cost savings or productivity gains from GPU-based AI uses outside the excluded rentals.
Assess the ongoing state using April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter ordinarily reportable before September 1. The speaker supplied no reporting period.
Read the future clause as an observation about evidence of prospective value available at publication, not a forecast with an invented deadline.
The rental exclusion defines scope; it is not a conditional forecast antecedent.
'Very little' concerns the broad economic contribution. One useful application does not by itself disprove it, and GPU sales alone do not establish benefits for end users.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence for the target period shows small economic benefits across the included GPU uses, with little credible evidence of scalable prospective benefits available at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, material and measured commercial or productivity benefits from included GPU uses, together with documented scalable applications, establish substantially more than very little economic value.
